questions.question: What body fields does POST /v1/customers accept, and what is the optional caller account field called?

questions.question: How do I fetch one v1 customer, and what prefix do v1 customer ids use?
questions.reference: Fetch one v1 customer with GET /v1/customers/{id}. Customer ids start with cus_.

questions.question: What are the v1 invoice status values?
questions.reference: The v1 invoice status values are draft, open, paid, and void.

questions.question: How do I move a v1 draft invoice to open?
questions.reference: Move a v1 draft invoice to open with POST /v1/invoices/{id}/finalize.

questions.question: How do I record usage in v1, and does quantity have to be a whole number?
questions.reference: Record v1 usage with POST /v1/usage_records. The field is metric and quantity must be a whole number.

questions.question: What is the v1 live rate limit?
questions.reference: On v1, live keys are allowed 100 requests per minute.

questions.question: What is the v1 test-key rate limit, and which header reports remaining requests?
questions.reference: v1 test keys are allowed 20 requests per minute. The remaining count is in X-RateLimit-Remaining.

questions.question: Which events can a v1 webhook subscribe to, and which header carries the signature?
questions.reference: v1 webhook events include invoice.paid, invoice.opened, and customer.created. The signature header is Northline-Signature.

questions.question: How long is the v1 webhook delivery timeout, and how many retries does v1 make?
questions.reference: v1 webhook delivery timeout is 10 seconds, and failed deliveries retry 3 times.

questions.question: How do I create a customer with the v1 Python SDK?
questions.reference: The v1 Python SDK calls northline.Customer.create and can send external_id.

questions.question: How do I create a customer with the v1 Node SDK?

questions.question: What body fields does POST /v2/customers accept, including the caller account field and the tax field?

questions.question: How do I update a v2 customer's billing address?
questions.reference: Update a v2 billing address with PATCH /v2/customers/{customer_id}.

questions.question: What are the v2 invoice status values?
questions.reference: The v2 invoice status values are draft, issued, settled, and void.

questions.question: How do I move a v2 draft invoice to issued?
questions.reference: Move a v2 draft to issued with POST /v2/invoices/{invoice_id}/issue.

questions.question: How do I record usage in v2, and what type is quantity?
questions.reference: Record v2 usage with POST /v2/usage_records. Send meter_id and a decimal string quantity.

questions.question: How do I list meters in v2?
questions.reference: List v2 meters with GET /v2/meters.

questions.question: What is the v2 live rate limit, and is there a burst allowance?
questions.reference: On v2, live keys are allowed 300 requests per minute, with a burst allowance of 50 requests.

questions.question: What is the v2 test-key rate limit, and which header reports remaining requests?
questions.reference: v2 test keys are allowed 60 requests per minute. The remaining count is in RateLimit-Remaining.

questions.question: Which events can a v2 webhook subscribe to, and which header carries the signature?
questions.reference: v2 webhook events include invoice.settled, invoice.issued, customer.created, and usage.recorded. The signature header is Northline-Signature-256.

questions.question: What is the v2 webhook timestamp tolerance, and how do I send a test event?
questions.reference: v2 webhook timestamp tolerance is 5 minutes. Send a test event with POST /v2/webhook_endpoints/{endpoint_id}/ping.

questions.question: How do I create a customer with the v2 Python SDK?
questions.reference: The v2 Python SDK constructs NorthlineClient and sends account_ref to client.customers.create.

questions.question: How do I create a customer with the v2 Node SDK?

questions.question: When moving from v1 to v2, what replaces external_id?

questions.question: How long does Northline store an Idempotency-Key, and what error is returned when the body changes?

For API version v1, the Northline docs say:

v1 customers

Create a customer with POST /v1/customers. The body fields are name (string, required), email (string, required), and external_id (string, optional). Fetch one customer with GET /v1/customers/{id}. List customers with GET /v1/customers. Customer ids start with cus_.

v1 does not accept a tax identifier or a billing address object. There is no PATCH method on v1 customers.

v1 does not accept a tax identifier or a billing address object. There is no PATCH method on v1 customers.

v1 usage records

Record usage with POST /v1/usage_records. The body fields are customer (required), metric (string, required, for example emails_sent), quantity (integer, required), and timestamp (unix seconds, optional). quantity must be a whole number in v1. v1 has no list method for usage records.

The field name metric is the v1 name of the thing you are counting.

v1 invoices

Create a draft invoice with POST /v1/invoices. The body fields are customer (customer id, required), currency (optional, default usd), and line_items (array of description and amount_cents). The status values are draft, open, paid, and void. Move a draft to open with POST /v1/invoices/{id}/finalize. Fetch one invoice with GET /v1/invoices/{id}.

amount_cents is an integer number of cents. A collected v1 invoice uses the status paid.

v1 webhooks

Create a webhook endpoint with POST /v1/webhook_endpoints. The body fields are url (required) and events (array, required). The event names are invoice.paid, invoice.opened, and customer.created. Northline signs the raw body and sends the hex digest in the header Northline-Signature. The digest is HMAC-SHA256, using the endpoint signing secret.

The signing secret is shown once at creation and is not published in these docs. Rotate it with POST /v1/webhook_endpoints/{id}/rotate_secret. Delivery timeout is 10 seconds. Failed deliveries retry 3 times.

A v1 endpoint does not emit the newer settled or issued event names.

Error codes

Every error body has the same shape: {"error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "doc_url": "..."}}.

Documented codes:
authentication_failed uses HTTP status 401.
rate_limited uses HTTP status 429.
parameter_unknown uses HTTP status 400 and means the body contains a field the endpoint does not accept.
resource_missing uses HTTP status 404.
idempotency_conflict uses HTTP status 409.

Clients should branch on the code string, not on the message text. Message wording can change between releases.

List endpoints accept limit and starting_after. limit defaults to 20 and the maximum is 100. starting_after is a cursor. Pass the id of the last object you received. The response has has_more, a boolean, and data, an array.

There is no offset parameter. Do not send page numbers. If has_more is false, you have reached the end of the list.

Idempotency

Send the Idempotency-Key header on create requests that must not run twice. Northline stores the key for 24 hours. Replaying the same key with the same body returns the original response. Replaying the same key with a different body returns error code idempotency_conflict.

Use a new key when the request body changes. Keys are opaque strings chosen by the client. The docs do not assign a key for you.

Error codes

Every error body has the same shape: {"error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "doc_url": "..."}}.

Documented codes:
authentication_failed uses HTTP status 401.
rate_limited uses HTTP status 429.
parameter_unknown uses HTTP status 400 and means the body contains a field the endpoint does not accept.
resource_missing uses HTTP status 404.
idempotency_conflict uses HTTP status 409.

Clients should branch on the code string, not on the message text. Message wording can change between releases.
